children: The House of Representatives passed a new Russia sanctions bill, paving the way for President Donald Trump to impose up to 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil and gas such as China and India.
The bill, called the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, passed the Senate vote last month and will now head to Trump's desk to be signed into law.
China is the top buyer of Russian crude, followed by India. To note, India is still negotiating a trade deal with the U.S., while China's President Xi Jinping is set to meet Trump next week.

"China opposes long-arm jurisdiction and unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and lack UN Security Council mandate," Guo Jiakun, spokesperson for China's foreign ministry, told reporters.
India said it remains committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4B people "through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics."
It added that New Delhi discussed the issue at high levels with U.S. interlocutors in recent months, flagging the implications for bilateral ties and the international energy market.

The bill's passage comes days after the BRICS Summit, where the organization's members condemned unilateral coercive measures in the form of economic and secondary sanctions. They did not name the U.S.

It's unlikely that the U.S. will escalate trade tensions with China ahead of Xi's visit next week. China's tendency to retaliate against U.S. sanctions would limit how far Trump's tariffs would go, Martin Chorzempa, senior fellow at the Peterson Institute for International Economics, told
Michael Kugelman, senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, told

that India built some insulation from U.S. tariff shocks through trade deals with the EU and elsewhere. "But [up to] 100% tariff from a critical export destination is real bad news, no matter how you slice it and even with successful hedging tactics."

title: China, India could face up to 100% U.S. tariffs for buying Russian oil
